sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: A small, often shrubby deciduous maple, about 4–15 m tall. Its opposite, leathery, glossy leaves are about 3–6 cm long and typically have three rounded, nearly entire lobes. Yellow-green flowers appear in hanging clusters in spring; paired samaras have nearly parallel wings. It grows in open woodland and on dry, rocky or calcareous slopes across the Mediterranean region east to Iran and Turkmenistan. The five-lobed leaf in the existing plate is atypical; five lobes can occur, but the illustration is not a strong species-level match.

sections.title: Food and safety
sections.text: A source describes tender maple leaves as edible at genus level, but does not establish that use specifically for this species; no species-specific food or toxicity claim is made here.
